name: Cartilage growth methods

card.summary: Online theories about stimulating nose and ear cartilage to grow in adulthood, aimed at reshaping a nose tip or ear without surgery.
card.note: Cartilage has limited regeneration; claimed methods are not backed by published trials in this use.

quick.overview:
Cartilage growth methods are looksmaxxing theories that adult nasal or ear cartilage can be coaxed to grow or remodel, so that features regarded as unfixable without surgery can be improved. The goal is a different nose or ear shape without hardmaxxing.

The central idea, laid out in a looksmax.org guide, separates appositional growth (adding layers on the outside) from interstitial growth (expanding from within).
quick.how: The forum guide discusses theory about elastic cartilage in the nose; people reading it consider adjusting habits they believe affect growth.
quick.risks: Cartilage has no blood supply and limited repair capacity, and no published trial tests these methods for nose or ear reshaping.

lead: Cartilage growth methods are theories from looksmaxxing forums that adult nose or ear cartilage can be stimulated to grow or remodel, so that features regarded as fixable only through surgery can be changed without it. The goal people describe is a different nose or ear shape, particularly the nasal structure, through habits and routines rather than an operation. A looksmax.org guide frames the nose as elastic cartilage and distinguishes appositional from interstitial growth. [1]

In biology, cartilage is a tissue without blood vessels or nerves that has limited repair capacity, and cell division in it is very slow. [2] Research on cartilage growth has mostly concerned development and joint disease, for example studies of progenitor cells at the surface of articular cartilage. [3] A 2022 scoping review of nasal septal cartilage found that growth is fastest in the first years of life and plateaus by early adulthood. [6]

The topic sits within 'softmaxxing' versus 'hardmaxxing': hardmaxxing covers surgery and other invasive options, and the guide positions cartilage growth as a way to approach features usually thought to need them. [1][9] No published trial has tested these methods for the nose or ears.

chain: Reshaped nose or ear without surgery
angle.text: Proponents hope to change nose-tip or ear shape without an operation by encouraging cartilage to grow. The approach is theoretical and tied to forum guides.

infobox: Elastic cartilage (outer ear, parts of the larynx) and nasal septal cartilage [5][6]

paras: The looksmax.org guide discusses elastic cartilage, describing appositional growth as layers added on top of existing cartilage, like snow piled onto a snowman, and interstitial growth as expansion from within. Its author says they have been 'experimenting and researching' ways to fix features regarded as unfixable without hardmaxxing, with nasal structure and the eye area as targets, and plans a separate guide on bone remodeling. [1]
Replies in the thread are brief; one user welcomes it and the author notes they rarely see 'nosemaxxing' threads elsewhere. [1] The material is a user's theory rather than a standardised protocol.

Proponents argue that features such as the nasal structure can be improved if cartilage can be induced to grow, and that the two growth patterns give a framework for how that might happen. [1] The guide says the nose is made of elastic cartilage, while anatomical sources describe elastic cartilage as the tissue of the outer ear and parts of the larynx and Eustachian tube. [5]

Cartilage lacks blood vessels and its cells are bound in lacunae and cannot migrate to damaged areas, which limits repair. [2] A progenitor cell population has been reported at the surface of articular (joint) cartilage that supports growth by apposition, a finding in joint tissue rather than nose or ear. [3]
Elastic cartilage contains elastic fibres within a matrix made by chondroblasts at the edge of the perichondrium; its cells make up only about 2% of its volume. [5]

The 2022 scoping review (86 articles, 1963-2021) reports that nasal septal growth is fastest in the first two years, plateaus by about age 20, and shows very limited proliferation up to about 35 in the anterior central septum. It also finds the cartilaginous area shrinking with age, attributed to ossification of part of the septum, and notes that the mechanisms and what drives growth are unresolved. [6]

Where surgeons change nasal or ear shape, they do so by reshaping cartilage directly: otoplasty uses stitches, scoring or removal of cartilage to set the ears back, and chin and nose procedures are often combined. [7][8]

No studies found for nose or ear reshaping. Related research examines cartilage in joints and growth plates, such as a randomised clinical trial of low-intensity ultrasound on knee cartilage thickness. [4] Laboratory and review work on nasal septal cartilage describes growth in childhood rather than stimulated growth in adults. [6]

lore.intro: A looksmax.org thread presents cartilage growth as a way to fix features seen as unmaxxable.[1]

claims.claim: Adult nose cartilage can be grown by appositional growth
claims.believers: The guide says cartilage forms layers on existing cartilage, like snow on a snowman.[1]
claims.experts: Cartilage divides slowly and has limited regeneration; no published studies have tested these methods for the nose.[2]

claims.claim: Interstitial growth can enlarge nasal cartilage from within
claims.believers: The guide lists interstitial growth as the second growth pattern and presents both as the basis for fixing 'unmaxxable' features. [1]
claims.experts: The scoping review reports very limited proliferation in the septum by early adulthood and unresolved mechanisms. [6]

claims.claim: Cartilage can be reshaped without surgery
claims.believers: Users say they want to fix features otherwise needing hardmaxxing. [1][9]
claims.experts: Surgeons reshape ear and chin tissue with sutures, scoring, removal or implants. [7][8] No published trial tests non-surgical reshaping.
